rationale: No country variable exists in the dictionary; the ISO3 code 'CHL' would be a constant assigned during harmonization, not derived from a raw variable.
Interview year is given by fecha_año (2015/2016), though the survey reference year (CASEN 2015) could also be hardcoded.
fecha_mes holds the interview month.
region is the first-level administrative division (regions of Chile).
zona codes 1=urbano, 2=rural and must be recoded to 1=urban, 0=rural.
folio uniquely identifies the household.
o is the person order number within the household; combined with folio it identifies the person.
expr is the regional expansion factor, the main weight in CASEN, and the only household-level candidate (expc is for self-represented comunas).
expr is the regional expansion factor applied to persons in CASEN.
varunit is the variance cluster (conglomerado), the closest to a primary sampling unit.
varstrat is the variance stratum used in the survey's sampling design, which matches the sampling stratum.

pco1 gives the relationship to the household head and must be recoded into head, spouse, child, other relative, non-relative and domestic worker; the domestic worker category may need the nucleo=0 code.
sexo already uses 1=male and 2=female.
edad is age in years.
ecivil can be recoded: soltero to single; casado, conviviente to union; anulado, separado, divorciado to divorced_or_separated; viudo to widowed.
r3 asks about belonging to an indigenous people, so any of codes 1-9 maps to indigenous and 10 to other; there is no afro-descendant category.
A person has a disability if any of the permanent or long-term condition variables is coded 1-6; code 7 means no condition.
r1a (nationality) and r1b (mother's residence at birth, including another country) identify international migrants, though the exact definition of migrant is a choice.
activ gives employed, unemployed and inactive; edad is used to flag those below working age, and activ may be missing for them. It could be rebuilt from o1, o2, o3, o6 and o5.
o15 gives the employment category in the main job (employer, own account, employee, unpaid family worker, domestic service, armed forces), which maps to the target categories.
oficio1 gives the 1-digit occupation code (CIUO-88 major groups) for the main job, which can be recoded into the 9 IDB occupation groups (oficio4 offers more detail).
rama1 gives the ISIC-based industry letter groups for the main job, which can be regrouped into the 9 IDB industry categories (rama1_sub covers the secondary job and is not needed).
o10 records usual weekly hours worked in the main job, with 999 as missing.
Hours worked in secondary jobs are not collected (only main-job hours in o10), so total weekly hours cannot be built.
o23 gives the number of people working in the firm, which can be categorized into small, medium and large.
o15 distinguishes public-sector employees (codes 3 and 4) from private-sector and other categories, so it identifies public-sector workers.
o16 gives contract duration (indefinite or fixed term) and o17 indicates whether a written contract exists, which together define contract type.
o29 records whether the person contributed to a pension system last month, with code 7 meaning not contributing.
o28 asks directly whether the person is affiliated to a pension system.
yoprcor is the corrected main-occupation income (wages plus independent earnings); alternatively sum the components y0101c and y0701c plus other main-job payments.

In-kind payments received in the main salaried job (food, vouchers, housing, vehicle, transport, etc.) are the non-monetary labor income of the main job; independent in-kind income (y0801) could also be added.
Income from secondary occupation is given separately for salaried (yosa) and independent (yosi) workers.

Total monetary labor income is the sum of monetary components of main job (salaried wages and allowances, bonuses, independent cash income) plus secondary job income; ytrabajocor or yoprcor are alternatives.
Non-monetary labor income combines in-kind salaried benefits, independent in-kind withdrawals, and own consumption of agricultural products.
Monetary non-labor income comprises rents, interest, transfers, remittances, pensions, subsidies and other non-labor receipts.

Contributory pensions are old-age, disability, widowhood, orphanhood and other pensions, excluding the solidarity basic pensions (y2601, y2604) and APS top-ups; APS-linked pensions (y260201) are included as they are contributory pensions with a supplement.
Money from relatives outside the household, within the country (yfa1) and abroad (yfa2); strictly remittances are mostly yfa2 but the schema may include both.
yaimh is the household imputed rent, with yaimcorh as the corrected version.
The dictionary has only the poverty classification (pobreza) and no poverty line value.
No extreme poverty line value is provided, only the pobreza category.
e3 asks whether the person currently attends an educational establishment (1=yes, 2=no), and the derived 'asiste' variable has the same coding, so either recodes to 0/1.
The derived 'esc' variable gives years of schooling directly; it could be rebuilt from e6a and e6b if needed.

Public institution is identified from the dependency of the establishment (e8 or depen/e7depen, with municipal, JUNJI, Integra and CRUCH universities counted as public), restricted to people who attend (e3).
v23 gives the water source (public network codes 1-3) and v24 the distribution system (tap inside the dwelling), which together define piped water access.
v23 records where the dwelling's water comes from (public network, well, river, tanker truck, other).
v26 records the dwelling's electricity source, but the survey does not ask specifically about the main lighting source, so having electricity from a public network or other source is used as a proxy.
v25 records the excreta disposal system (WC to sewer, septic tank, latrine, none), which maps to the sanitation facility categories.
v4 gives the predominant floor material.
v2 gives the predominant material of the exterior walls.
v6 gives the predominant roof material.
v32a gives the number of bedrooms used exclusively for sleeping that the household occupies (v29a is the dwelling total, but the household-level count is preferred).
The survey only records bedrooms and bathrooms (v29a/b, v32a/b), not the total number of rooms in the dwelling.
v12 gives the household's tenure of the dwelling: owned codes 1-4 map to 1, rented codes 5-6 to 0, and irregular occupation code 10 to 3.
Fixed and mobile broadband access items (r15a-r15d) indicate whether the household has an internet connection; r15e and r15f refer to devices.
r20 records whether the person has a working mobile phone (prepaid or contract); the household flag is built by aggregating it over members.
r14d asks whether the nucleus has a working computer.
No question on refrigerator ownership appears in the dictionary; r14 covers only water heater, landline, pay TV, computer and smart TV.
r13b counts private-use vehicles in the nucleus (r12 is the ownership screen); auto_ch is 1 if r13b > 0.
